tool_analysis:
1) Step Analysis / What the recorded steps accomplish
- Navigate from about:blank to the Magento admin Sales Orders URL.
- Detect and analyze the Magento Admin login page.
- Log in with username=admin and password=password123 using index-based inputs (element_hash recorded) rather than the previously failing CSS selector input[name="login[username]"][type="text"].
- After login, land directly on the Sales > Orders grid at /admin/sales_order/.
- Analyze the grid page thoroughly, mapping filters, export controls, pagination, and mass actions; confirm that the export UI consists of an "Export to:" dropdown and an "Export" button, along with toolbar Search/Reset Filter.
- Derive numeric indexes for major interactive controls: export dropdown is semantic_role=export_format_dropdown (index 6 in the final mapping), export button semantic_role=export_submit_button (index 7), Search button (index 9), Order # filter text input (index 23), etc.
- Attempt to interact with export dropdown and button using the numeric index abstraction, but the final step shows that index 6/7 refer to <a> elements, not a real <select>, and clicking index 7 actually hits a "Terms and conditions" button—indicating that index-based generic mapping is unreliable without CSS selectors.

2) Task Definition / Tool Purpose
Create a robust, reusable automation tool that:
- Navigates to the Magento Admin login page if needed.
- Logs in with provided credentials.
- Navigates to the Sales > Orders grid.
- Optionally applies a simple filter (Order #) on the grid.
- Selects an export format (CSV, Excel, or XML) from the actual export <select> control in the toolbar.
- Clicks the Export button to trigger the download of the current (possibly filtered) orders grid.

This must address the specific previous failures:
- The blank-page / missing-login-field problem due to an over-specific CSS selector.
- The original tool used input[name='login[username]'][type='text'], which failed when that exact selector was not present (environment issues). We now have confirmed working index-based inputs with element_hash for username, password, and login button.

3) Action Plan / To-do list for tool steps
A. Login/navigation phase
1) navigation: Go directly to the Sales Orders URL /index.php/admin/sales_order/ (as in the recording). Magento will redirect to login page if not authenticated.
2) input (username): Use the stable index/element_hash pair for the username input (highlight_index 1, tag=input, element_hash 3597a5c5e6). Input {username}.
3) input (password): Use the stable index/element_hash pair for the password input (highlight_index 3, element_hash 1c47a5217e). Input {password}.
4) click (login): Click the Login button using the element with highlight_index 5, element_hash 6831836d17.
5) wait: Allow a few seconds for login and redirect to the Orders grid.
6) navigation: After authentication, explicitly navigate to /index.php/admin/sales_order/ again to ensure we are on the Sales > Orders grid. (Magento typically already sends us there, but navigation is deterministic.)

B. Filtering phase (optional from business perspective, but supported by tool)
7) If an order_increment_id filter value is provided (non-empty string), input it into the Order # filter field in the filter row. The analysis identified this as:
   - semantic_role: filter_order_increment_id with index 23 in mapping, and earlier selector hints indicated this is input[name='increment_id'] within table#sales_order_grid thead.
   For determinism, use a CSS selector like: "table#sales_order_grid thead input[name='increment_id']" in an input step.
8) If a filter was applied in step 7, click the Search button in the toolbar to apply filters. Toolbar mapping shows Search as a button with visible text "Search" (semantic_role filters_apply_button, index 9). Prefer a robust CSS selector: "button[title='Search']".
9) wait: Brief delay for the grid to reload with filtered results.

C. Export phase (core of the tool)
10) select_change: Choose the export format in the "Export to:" dropdown. From earlier HTML inference and analysis, this is likely "select#sales_order_grid_export". Use a select_change step with cssSelector "select#sales_order_grid_export" and selectedText={export_format}.
11) click: Activate the Export button using a reliable toolbar selector, e.g. "button[title='Export']".
12) wait: Wait a few seconds for server to generate and start downloading the file. (The tool framework might not capture the file, but this delay ensures the action completes.)
13) Optionally extract_page_content or simply end; since the goal is side-effect (download), page extraction is not required.

4) Variable Identification / Input parameters
From the flows and environment:
- username (string, required): Admin username for login. Default in description: "admin". Required because Magento admin requires a login.
- password (string, required): Admin password. The task description specifies password123. Required.
- order_increment_id (string, optional): Value to put into the Order # filter. If empty, skip filter steps and export the full grid. This matches user’s earlier attempt where it could be empty.
- export_format (string, required, enum: ["CSV", "Excel", "XML"]): Visible text of the option to select in Export to dropdown. Prior analyses show exactly these three.

No other parameters are essential to the core task of exporting. Pagination, other filters, mass actions are outside the core scope and therefore not added as input parameters per instructions.

5) Step Optimization / Determinism
- Navigation optimization: Start directly at /index.php/admin/sales_order/ as in the session; Magento will route to login if not already authed. Then after login, navigate (or remain) at that same URL. No need to go through /index.php/admin/ separately.
- Login selector robustness: Use element_hash-based click/input steps instead of brittle CSS names. The session recorded element_hash values for username, password, and Login button on the Magento Admin 1.x login page:
  - Username: input, highlight_index 1, element_hash 3597a5c5e6
  - Password: input, highlight_index 3, element_hash 1c47a5217e
  - Login button: input, highlight_index 5, element_hash 6831836d17
  These are more reliable than the previously failing CSS selector.
- Export controls selectors: Instead of ambiguous index-based references (which misfired in the session when the select_change step thought index 6 was a select but it was actually an <a>), use semantic CSS selectors derived from the page analysis:
  - Export dropdown: select#sales_order_grid_export
  - Export button: button[title='Export']
  - Order # filter: table#sales_order_grid thead input[name='increment_id']
  - Search button: button[title='Search']
  These selectors should resolve to exactly one element on the Orders grid page and avoid the prior index confusion.
- Agentic vs deterministic steps: All interactions here can be deterministic via navigation/input/select/click with robust CSS. No agent steps are strictly required. We avoid agent steps to keep the tool deterministic.
- URL manipulation (optional pass): Magento’s grid filtering is likely implemented via GET parameters (e.g., ?order_increment_id=...). However, we do not have explicit confirmation of parameter names, and interacting with the actual filter inputs is reliable and already well-specified. For exports, the action is a POST/form submit; direct URL editing would be brittle. Therefore, do not replace UI filtering/export steps with URL operations.

Given the previous tool failure (waiting for login field with wrong selector), the critical fixes are:
- Use element_hash-backed input/click for login instead of CSS selector.
- Use clear CSS selectors for export dropdown and button instead of index-based generic steps.
- Parameterize export format and optional Order # filter via {export_format} and {order_increment_id}.

This yields a single-purpose, deterministic tool that logs in and exports the current (optionally filtered) Orders grid.
name: tool_export_orders.v3
description: Logs into Magento Admin and exports the current (optionally filtered) Sales > Orders grid to CSV, Excel, or XML using robust selectors and avoiding the previously failing login selector. Assumes Magento 1.x-style admin at /index.php/admin/ with Sales > Orders grid at /index.php/admin/sales_order/.

steps.description: Navigate directly to the Magento Sales Orders admin URL; Magento will redirect to login if not authenticated.
Enter the Magento Admin username into the username field on the login form.
Enter the Magento Admin password into the password field on the login form.
Click the Login button to submit the Magento Admin login form.
Wait for the login request to complete and for Magento to load the admin interface.
Ensure we are on the Sales > Orders grid page after login by navigating directly to the Sales Orders URL.
If order_increment_id is non-empty, type it into the Order # filter field in the Orders grid header row. If empty, this will effectively do nothing useful but is harmless.
Click the Search button in the Orders grid toolbar to apply the current filters (including Order # if provided).
Wait for the Orders grid to reload with the applied filter (if any).
In the Orders grid toolbar, select the desired export format (CSV, Excel, or XML) from the 'Export to' dropdown.
Click the Export button to export the current Orders grid (filtered or unfiltered) in the selected format.
Wait for Magento to process the export request and initiate the file download.

input_schema.name: username
input_schema.description: Magento Admin username to log in with (e.g., 'admin').

input_schema.name: password
input_schema.description: Magento Admin password for the given username (e.g., 'password123').

input_schema.name: order_increment_id
input_schema.description: Exact Order # to filter by in the Orders grid. Leave empty string to export all orders without filtering.

input_schema.name: export_format
input_schema.description: Visible text of export format option in the 'Export to' dropdown on the Orders grid toolbar.
